'''Gil Chaverri Rodríguez''' (March 15, 1921, in [[Heredia, Costa Rica|Heredia]], [[Costa Rica]] – May 27, 2005, in [[San José, Costa Rica]]) was a Costa Rican chemist and physicist. Chaverri created an original arrangement of the [[periodic table]] of [[chemical elements]], published in 1952 in the ''[[Journal of Chemical Education]]''.<ref name="Ponchner"/><ref name="Mazurs">{{Cite book |last1=Mazurs|first1=Edward G.| title = Graphic Representations of the Periodic System during One Hundred Years | publisher = [[University of Alabama Press]] | year = 1974 | page = 209 | isbn = 0-8173-3200-6 }}</ref><ref name="Chaverri">{{cite journal|last1=Chaverri|first1=Gil R.|title=The periodic table of elements|journal=Journal of Chemical Education|date=December 1953|volume=30|issue=12|pages=632|doi=10.1021/ed030p632|bibcode=1953JChEd..30..632C}}</ref> His arrangement of the periodic table was based on the electronic structure of each element,<ref name="Químicos">{{cite web|title=1951 Rodríguez Tabla Periódica de los Elementos Químicos|url=http://www.meta-synthesis.com/webbook/35_pt/pt_database.php?PT_id=397|website=The INTERNET Database of Periodic Tables|accessdate=18 July 2017}}</ref> and was used in Costa Rican schools.<ref name="Ponchner">{{cite news|last1=Ponchner|first1=Debbie|title=Gil Chaverri Rodríguez Murió el 'papá' de la tabla periódica|url=http://wvw.nacion.com/ln_ee/2005/mayo/28/obituario0.html|accessdate=18 July 2017|work=Nacion|date=May 28, 2005}}</ref>

==Childhood and early education==
José Gil Chaverri Rodriguez was born in [[Heredia, Costa Rica]] on March 15, 1921, to  José Joaquín Chaverri Zúñiga and María Josefa Rodríguez Solera.<ref name="Ponchner"/> His family later moved to [[San José, Costa Rica|San José]], where he attended primary school at Escuela Buenaventura Corrales (1928-1933<ref name="CV"/>) and secondary school at the Colegio Seminario de San José (Seminary School, 1934-1937<ref name="CV"/>) and the Liceo de Costa Rica (1938-1939<ref name="CV"/>).<ref name="Polini"/><ref name="Ponchner"/>

==University education==
At the [[University of Costa Rica]] he earned a degree in agricultural engineering from the Faculty of Agronomy in 1944.
He went from there to [[Cornell University]], where he received a Masters in Sciences in 1945.<ref name="Polini"/><ref name="Ponchner"/><ref name="CV">{{cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae Gil Chaverri Rodríguez|url=https://gilchaverri.com/curriculum.html|website=Gil Chaverri Rodríguez|accessdate=19 July 2017}}</ref>
He also studied engineering at the University of Costa Rica from 1955-1957.<ref name="CV"/>

In 1959, he received a scholarship from the [[National Academy of Sciences]] of the [[United States]], which enabled him to attend [[Iowa State University]].<ref name="Polini"/> There he completed a Ph.D. thesis on the ''Application of the solubility-product principle to the dissolution of phosphate rock'' in 1962.<ref name="Chaverri Rodriguez">{{cite book|last1= Chaverri Rodriguez |first1=José Gil|title=Application of the solubility-product principle to the dissolution of phosphate rock|date=1962|publisher=Iowa State University|location=Ames, Iowa|url=http://lib.dr.iastate.edu/rtd/1998|accessdate=19 July 2017}}</ref>

In addition to his scientific studies, he was a gifted linguist, reading and speaking English, French and German by the time he finished high school, and later studying Russian, Latin, Greek, Italian and Portuguese.<ref name="Polini">{{cite journal|last1=Familia Chaverri Polini|title=Gil Chaverri Rodríguez Primer director del CIA|journal=Agronomía Costarricense|date=2005|volume=29 |issue=3|page=15|url=http://www.mag.go.cr/rev_agr/v29n03_015.pdf|accessdate=19 July 2017}}</ref>

==Career==
Gil Chaverri Rodriguez began teaching in 1942, at the Colegio Seminario.<ref name="Ponchner"/> 
From 1946-1978<ref name="CV"/> he taught chemistry at the University of Costa Rica, where he held a number of position. He was head of the Chemical Laboratory of the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (Laboratorio Químico del Ministerio de Agricultura y Ganadería) from 1948-1956. He was the founding Director of the Center for Agronomic Research (Centro de Investigación Agronómica, CIA) from 1956-1960, and Dean of the Faculty of Sciences and Letters from 1965-1971. 
He published both educational and scientific works, including textbooks such as 
''Ley de acción de masas y sus aplicaciones'' ("Law of mass action and its applications", 1950).<ref name="Ponchner"/><ref name="Polini"/><ref name="CV"/> 
From 1978 to 1999 he taught at the [[Universidad de Ciencias Médicas|Escuela Autónoma de Ciencias Médicas]].<ref name="CV"/> He retired in 1999.<ref name="Ponchner"/>

==Periodic Table==
Chaverri Rodríguez created an arrangement of the Periodic Table of Chemical Elements, published in 1952 in the ''Journal of Chemical Education''. His arrangement is based on the electronic structure of the elements, which allows for the placement of the [[lanthanide]] and [[actinide]] series in a logical sequence according to their atomic number. It has been used for teaching chemistry in Costa Rican schools.<ref name="Mazurs"/><ref name="Chaverri"/>

==Personal==
Chaverri Rodríguez was married to Antonieta Polini Castro, with whom he lived in  the San Antonio district of the [[Desamparados (canton)|Desamparados]] [[Cantons of Costa Rica|canton]] of [[San José, Costa Rica|San José]]. They had seven children. His wife predeceased him by two years.<ref name="Ponchner"/>

Gil Chaverri Rodríguez died at the [[Hospital México]], [[San José, Costa Rica]] on May 27, 2005.  Although he had suffered from [[Parkinson's disease]] for some time, the immediate cause of death was a heart attack.<ref name="Ponchner"/>
